newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dollar ends weaker on broad-based selling.
newsitem.headline: Canada dollar ends weaker on broad-based selling.

text.p: FORECAST RANGE 1.3750/1.3835 ASIAN CLOSE 1.3778
RESISTANCE 1.3712 SUPPORT 1.3862 HI 1.3789 LO 1.3755
CANADA OPEN 1.3757/62 HI 1.3833 EUROPE OPEN 1.3772

* Canada's dollar ended weaker on Wednesday at C$1.3823 (US$0.7234) from Tuesday's close of C$1.3787 (US$0.7253) on broad-based, but thin selling, dealers said. * They said the currency weakened to levels not seen since the Bank of Canada hiked its target ceiling for the overnight financing rate to 3.50 percent on June 26.

Nasato said the currency has had significant support around the C$1.3820 (US$0.7235) area and was not expected to weaken past C$1.3850 (US$0.7220), even if the Bank of Canada failed to support the unit by intervening or a rate hike.

Traders also said speculation of an imminent rate hike in the U.S. may have intensified pressure on the Canadian dollar after Federal Reserve policymakers warned of the risk of higher inflation in the U.S. economy.
Fed policymakers echoed Greenspan's comments to the Congressional panel on banking that the economy's performance was outstanding, but said the Fed must remain vigilant.

"The economy as a whole is functioning amazingly well," Fed Vice Chair Alice Rivlin told the House Banking Committee. "The overriding objective -- shared by all participants in the economy -- is to keep the good news flowing." She added that all Federal Open Market Commitee members agreed that the risk of faster inflation was "somewhat greater" than the risk of recession.
New York Fed President William McDonough said the key now was to avoid allowing the economy to avoid a boom-bust cycle.
"A U.S. rate hike would be negative for the Canadian dollar because it would lure capital flows away from Canada.
A U.S. rate hike would also put pressure on the Bank of Canada to raise interest rates here.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar fell against the German mark to 1.3174 markets from 1.3222 marks at Tuesday's close. The unit rose to 83.53 yen from 83.45 yen.
((Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100))
